subject: Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working
parts:
Currently, I'm testing metropolis against the binormal model. For metropolis with dense metric, the results are at the bottom of this email; the stepsize just keeps growing.

I think the problem may be coming from the way I'm treating prop_cov. Currently, it's being treated as if it were the covariance matrix, but is it actually the covariance matrix or its inverse?

If it is the inverse, then shouldn't the propose method for dense metropolis  look like
      void propose(std::vector<double>& q,
                   BaseRNG& rng) {
        Eigen::VectorXd init(q.size());
        for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
           init(i) = q[i];

        Eigen::VectorXd prop(q.size());
        prop = this->_nom_epsilon 
          * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

        for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
          q[i] = prop(i);
      }
where we have 

       prop = this->_nom_epsilon 
          * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

instead of

prop = this->_nom_epsilon * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov, this->_rand_int);
After running the former propose method, we get better results, but the step-size still seems to be increasing as it was previously.

This may have something to do with the init_stepsize() method in base_metro.hpp:
      void init_stepsize() {
        std::vector<double> params_r0(_params_r);
        std::vector<int> params_i0(_params_i);

        this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
        double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

        this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);        

        double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
        double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

        int direction = delta_log_p > log(0.5) ? 1 : -1;
        while (1) {    

          this->seed(params_r0, params_i0);

          this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
          double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

          this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);        

          double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
          double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

          if ((direction == 1) && !(delta_log_p > std::log(0.5)))
            break;
          else if ((direction == -1) && !(delta_log_p < std::log(0.5)))
            break;
          else
            this->_nom_epsilon = ( (direction == 1)
                                   ? 2.0 * this->_nom_epsilon
                                   : 0.5 * this->_nom_epsilon );

          if (this->_nom_epsilon > 1e300)
            throw std::runtime_error("Posterior is improper. Please check your model.");
          if (this->_nom_epsilon == 0)
            throw std::runtime_error("No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?");
        }        
      }
Should the line
          double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
actually be
          double delta_log_p = log_p - log_p0;
It was originally the former to mirror the init_stepsize in base_hmc.hpp; I believe the latter gives better results:

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working
parts:
There's a lot of literature out there on how Metropolis
works. I'd suggest looking it up and making sure your
implementation matches.

You are going to be estimating covariance. But whether you
take the inverse or not before plugging it into your
multivariate normal RNG depends on how you generate random
numbers (looks like you're using multi_normal_rng, which you
wrote, I believe). Whatever you do, make sure you don't have to do
matrix solving at each iteration --- if you do need to solve,
make sure to do it only once.

Also, you aren't going to be estimating step size and covariance
here (well, you could), but it's not like HMC where there's a number
of steps (corresponding to time intervals).

- Bob

On 5/21/13 4:01 PM, Peter Li wrote:
> Currently, I'm testing metropolis against the binormal model. For metropolis with dense metric, the results are at the
> bottom of this email; the stepsize just keeps growing.
>
> I think the problem may be coming from the way I'm treating prop_cov. Currently, it's being treated as if it were the
> covariance matrix, but is it actually the covariance matrix or its inverse?
>
> If it is the inverse, then shouldn't the propose method for dense metropolis look like
>
> | void propose(std::vector<double>& q,
> BaseRNG& rng) {
> Eigen::VectorXd init(q.size());
> for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
> init(i) = q[i];
>
> Eigen::VectorXd prop(q.size());
> prop = this->_nom_epsilon
> * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);
>
> for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
> q[i] = prop(i);
> }|
>
> where we have
>
> | prop = this->_nom_epsilon
> * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);
>
> |
>
>
> instead of
>
> |prop = this->_nom_epsilon * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov, this->_rand_int); |
> After running the former propose method, we get better results, but the step-size still seems to be increasing as it was
> previously.
>
> This may have something to do with the init_stepsize() method in base_metro.hpp:
>
> | void init_stepsize() {
> std::vector<double> params_r0(_params_r);
> std::vector<int> params_i0(_params_i);
>
> this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
> double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
>
> this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
>
> double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
> double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
>
> int direction = delta_log_p > log(0.5) ? 1 : -1;
> while (1) {
>
> this->seed(params_r0, params_i0);
>
> this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
> double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
>
> this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
>
> double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
> double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
>
> if ((direction == 1) && !(delta_log_p > std::log(0.5)))
> break;
> else if ((direction == -1) && !(delta_log_p < std::log(0.5)))
> break;
> else
> this->_nom_epsilon = ( (direction == 1)
> ? 2.0 * this->_nom_epsilon
> : 0.5 * this->_nom_epsilon );
>
> if (this->_nom_epsilon > 1e300)
> throw std::runtime_error("Posterior is improper. Please check your model.");
> if (this->_nom_epsilon == 0)
> throw std::runtime_error("No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?");
> }
> }|
>
> Should the line
>
> | double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
> |
>
> actually be
>
> | double delta_log_p = log_p - log_p0;|

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working
parts:
Just for curiosity, does one of those 3 (unit_metro, diag_metro or full matrix) use the algorithm proposed by Hario et al or something similar?

A while ago I used this one and the results weren't bad, they also propose a form of calculating the (adaptative) proposal covariance matrix without the need to recalculate the correlation of all other steps for every step. But for it work, I found necessary to use greedy adaptation in the begging, that is, use only the accepted steps for updating the proposal's distribution covariance matrix.

On 13-05-21 05:19 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
There's a lot of literature out there on how Metropolis
works.  I'd suggest looking it up and making sure your
implementation matches.

You are going to be estimating covariance.  But whether you
take the inverse or not before plugging it into your
multivariate normal RNG depends on how you generate random
numbers (looks like you're using multi_normal_rng, which you
wrote, I believe).  Whatever you do, make sure you don't have to do
matrix solving at each iteration --- if you do need to solve,
make sure to do it only once.

Also, you aren't going to be estimating step size and covariance
here (well, you could), but it's not like HMC where there's a number
of steps (corresponding to time intervals).

- Bob

On 5/21/13 4:01 PM, Peter Li wrote:
Currently, I'm testing metropolis against the binormal model. For metropolis with dense metric, the results are at the
bottom of this email; the stepsize just keeps growing.

I think the problem may be coming from the way I'm treating prop_cov. Currently, it's being treated as if it were the
covariance matrix, but is it actually the covariance matrix or its inverse?

If it is the inverse, then shouldn't the propose method for dense metropolis  look like

|       void propose(std::vector<double>& q,
                    BaseRNG& rng) {
         Eigen::VectorXd init(q.size());
         for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
            init(i) = q[i];

         Eigen::VectorXd prop(q.size());
         prop = this->_nom_epsilon
           * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

         for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
           q[i] = prop(i);
       }|

where we have

|        prop = this->_nom_epsilon
           * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

|


instead of

|prop = this->_nom_epsilon * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov, this->_rand_int); |
After running the former propose method, we get better results, but the step-size still seems to be increasing as it was
previously.

This may have something to do with the init_stepsize() method in base_metro.hpp:

|       void init_stepsize() {
         std::vector<double> params_r0(_params_r);
         std::vector<int> params_i0(_params_i);

         this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
         double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

         this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);

         double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
         double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

         int direction = delta_log_p > log(0.5) ? 1 : -1;
         while (1) {

           this->seed(params_r0, params_i0);

           this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
           double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

           this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);

           double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
           double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

           if ((direction == 1) && !(delta_log_p > std::log(0.5)))
             break;
           else if ((direction == -1) && !(delta_log_p < std::log(0.5)))
             break;
           else
             this->_nom_epsilon = ( (direction == 1)
                                    ? 2.0 * this->_nom_epsilon
                                    : 0.5 * this->_nom_epsilon );

           if (this->_nom_epsilon > 1e300)
             throw std::runtime_error("Posterior is improper. Please check your model.");
           if (this->_nom_epsilon == 0)
             throw std::runtime_error("No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?");
         }
       }|

Should the line

|           double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
|

actually be

|           double delta_log_p = log_p - log_p0;|

It was originally the former to mirror the init_stepsize in base_hmc.hpp; I believe the latter gives better results:

parts:
Thanks for the reference.

We're currently adapting in blocks, just like we do for HMC.
This is partly for stability and partly to avoid the overhead
matrix solvers running at every iteration during warmup.

- Bob

On 5/21/13 4:46 PM, Marco Inacio wrote:
> Just for curiosity, does one of those 3 (unit_metro, diag_metro or full matrix) use the algorithm proposed by Hario et
> al <http://www.math.unm.edu/%7Emichele/Teaching/SC/material/Haario2001_adaptiveMCMC.pdf> or something similar?

>
> A while ago I used this one and the results weren't bad, they also propose a form of calculating the (adaptative)
> proposal covariance matrix without the need to recalculate the correlation of all other steps for every step. But for it
> work, I found necessary to use greedy adaptation in the begging, that is, use only the accepted steps for updating the
> proposal's distribution covariance matrix.
>
> On 13-05-21 05:19 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
>> There's a lot of literature out there on how Metropolis
>> works. I'd suggest looking it up and making sure your
>> implementation matches.
>>
>> You are going to be estimating covariance. But whether you
>> take the inverse or not before plugging it into your
>> multivariate normal RNG depends on how you generate random
>> numbers (looks like you're using multi_normal_rng, which you
>> wrote, I believe). Whatever you do, make sure you don't have to do
>> matrix solving at each iteration --- if you do need to solve,
>> make sure to do it only once.
>>
>> Also, you aren't going to be estimating step size and covariance
>> here (well, you could), but it's not like HMC where there's a number
>> of steps (corresponding to time intervals).
>>
>> - Bob
>>
>> On 5/21/13 4:01 PM, Peter Li wrote:
>>> Currently, I'm testing metropolis against the binormal model. For metropolis with dense metric, the results are at the

>>> covariance matrix, but is it actually the covariance matrix or its inverse?

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working
parts:
As Bob noted, whether to use the covariance or its inverse depends on how you generate the proposal. Because we want to avoid unnecessary matrix ops I would compute the proposal by hand. In particular,

1. Compute Cholesky decomposition of the covariance.
2. Sample a vector of N(0, 1) variates, z.
3. Solve L dx = z for dx.
4. x_{propose} = x_{current} + dx

You were also correct about the init stepsize - it should be log(target accept) = log p_{propose} - log p_{current}. Make sure it's consistent here and in the actual transition!

To debug, start with a simple Gaussian model with known covariance. Then make sure Metropolis works with no adaptation, then with stepsize adaptation, then finally with stepsize and covariance adaptation. The latter is eased by knowing what the true covariance should be.

Also watch the log posterior after each iteration. If you have the accept stat wrong then the log prob will shrink during convergence instead of grow.

parts: We don't use a scheme like Haario, for reasons Bob mentioned and more.  We do use the banana for testing, though!

On May 21, 2013, at 9:46 PM, Marco Inacio <marcoig...@gmail.com> wrote:

Just for curiosity, does one of those 3 (unit_metro, diag_metro or full matrix) use the algorithm proposed by Hario et al or something similar?

A while ago I used this one and the results weren't bad, they also propose a form of calculating the (adaptative) proposal covariance matrix without the need to recalculate the correlation of all other steps for every step. But for it work, I found necessary to use greedy adaptation in the begging, that is, use only the accepted steps for updating the proposal's distribution covariance matrix.

On 13-05-21 05:19 PM, Bob Carpenter wrote:
There's a lot of literature out there on how Metropolis
works.  I'd suggest looking it up and making sure your
implementation matches.

You are going to be estimating covariance.  But whether you
take the inverse or not before plugging it into your
multivariate normal RNG depends on how you generate random
numbers (looks like you're using multi_normal_rng, which you
wrote, I believe).  Whatever you do, make sure you don't have to do
matrix solving at each iteration --- if you do need to solve,
make sure to do it only once.

Also, you aren't going to be estimating step size and covariance
here (well, you could), but it's not like HMC where there's a number
of steps (corresponding to time intervals).

- Bob

On 5/21/13 4:01 PM, Peter Li wrote:
Currently, I'm testing metropolis against the binormal model. For metropolis with dense metric, the results are at the
bottom of this email; the stepsize just keeps growing.

I think the problem may be coming from the way I'm treating prop_cov. Currently, it's being treated as if it were the
covariance matrix, but is it actually the covariance matrix or its inverse?

If it is the inverse, then shouldn't the propose method for dense metropolis  look like

|       void propose(std::vector<double>& q,
                    BaseRNG& rng) {
         Eigen::VectorXd init(q.size());
         for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
            init(i) = q[i];

         Eigen::VectorXd prop(q.size());
         prop = this->_nom_epsilon
           * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

         for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
           q[i] = prop(i);
       }|

where we have

|        prop = this->_nom_epsilon
           * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov.inverse(), this->_rand_int);

|


instead of

|prop = this->_nom_epsilon * stan::prob::multi_normal_rng(init, _prop_cov, this->_rand_int); |
After running the former propose method, we get better results, but the step-size still seems to be increasing as it was
previously.

This may have something to do with the init_stepsize() method in base_metro.hpp:

|       void init_stepsize() {
         std::vector<double> params_r0(_params_r);
         std::vector<int> params_i0(_params_i);

         this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
         double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

         this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);

         double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
         double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

         int direction = delta_log_p > log(0.5) ? 1 : -1;
         while (1) {

           this->seed(params_r0, params_i0);

           this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);
           double log_p0 = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);

           this->propose(_params_r, _rand_int);

           double log_p = log_prob(_params_r, _params_i);
           double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;

           if ((direction == 1) && !(delta_log_p > std::log(0.5)))
             break;
           else if ((direction == -1) && !(delta_log_p < std::log(0.5)))
             break;
           else
             this->_nom_epsilon = ( (direction == 1)
                                    ? 2.0 * this->_nom_epsilon
                                    : 0.5 * this->_nom_epsilon );

           if (this->_nom_epsilon > 1e300)
             throw std::runtime_error("Posterior is improper. Please check your model.");
           if (this->_nom_epsilon == 0)
             throw std::runtime_error("No acceptably small step size could be found. Perhaps the posterior is not continuous?");
         }
       }|

Should the line

|           double delta_log_p = log_p0 - log_p;
|

actually be

|           double delta_log_p = log_p - log_p0;|

It was originally the former to mirror the init_stepsize in base_hmc.hpp; I believe the latter gives better results:

messages.author: 839dfa09184985a5
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Dense Metropolis (and potentially diag metro) not working
parts:
Thanks a lot. I think everything is working now--I'm going to run some
more of the BUGS models to make sure.


Peter

On 5/21/13 5:25 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:
> As Bob noted, whether to use the covariance or its inverse depends on how you generate the proposal. Because we want to avoid unnecessary matrix ops I would compute the proposal by hand. In particular,
>
> 1. Compute Cholesky decomposition of the covariance.
> 2. Sample a vector of N(0, 1) variates, z.
> 3. Solve L dx = z for dx.
> 4. x_{propose} = x_{current} + dx

This is how the multi_normal_rng that I created works. The problem
before was that I was multiplying by the stepsize last for some reason,
so x_{current} was being multiplied by the step-size too, so all the
proposals were larger than they should've been and I guess that's what
caused metropolis to get stuck.

>
> You were also correct about the init stepsize - it should be log(target accept) = log p_{propose} - log p_{current}. Make sure it's consistent here and in the actual transition!
>
> To debug, start with a simple Gaussian model with known covariance. Then make sure Metropolis works with no adaptation, then with stepsize adaptation, then finally with stepsize and covariance adaptation. The latter is eased by knowing what the true covariance should be.
>
> Also watch the log posterior after each iteration. If you have the accept stat wrong then the log prob will shrink during convergence instead of grow.
>

parts:
How does step-size factor into this? For dense metro, I have what's below. Is this the correct way to treat step-size?

      void propose(std::vector<double>& q,
                   BaseRNG& rng) {
        Eigen::VectorXd prop(q.size());

        for(size_t  i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)
          prop(i) = stan::prob::normal_rng(0,
                                           this->_nom_epsilon, 
                                           rng);

        prop = _prop * prop;

        for(size_t i = 0; i < q.size(); i++)

where _prop is 
          this->_prop = this->_prop_cov.inverse().llt().matrixL();
On 5/21/13 5:25 PM, Michael Betancourt wrote:

As Bob noted, whether to use the covariance or its inverse depends on how you generate the proposal.  Because we want to avoid unnecessary matrix ops I would compute the proposal by hand.  In particular,

1. Compute Cholesky decomposition of the covariance.
2. Sample a vector of N(0, 1) variates, z.
3. Solve L dx = z for dx.
4.  x_{propose} = x_{current} + dx

You were also correct about the init stepsize - it should be log(target accept) = log p_{propose} - log p_{current}.  Make sure it's consistent here and in the actual transition!  

To debug, start with a simple Gaussian model with known covariance.  Then make sure Metropolis works with no adaptation, then with stepsize adaptation, then finally with stepsize and covariance adaptation.  The latter is eased by knowing what the true covariance should be.

Also watch the log posterior after each iteration.  If you have the accept stat wrong then the log prob will shrink during convergence instead of grow.
